text: Now let's actually group rows together — group by.

This is the PySpark version of Pandas' group by from Lesson 26 — same idea, almost the same name. But try showing it directly and it fails: group by alone returns a grouped data object, not a DataFrame. It's a statement of intent, waiting for you to say what to actually calculate.

Count is the simplest way to complete that thought — how many rows landed in each group. Chaining it directly onto group by turns the intent into an actual, showable DataFrame — vendor I-D, and a count.
And you can group by more than one column at once — every distinct combination becomes its own group, with its own row and count.
Group by states the intent, count completes it. Next lesson: aggregations — sums, averages, and more, per group.
